newsitem.title: ITALY: Pope comforts widow of executed American.
newsitem.headline: Pope comforts widow of executed American.

text.p: The body of Joseph O'Dell, a convicted murderer and rapist executed last week in the United States, arrived to be buried in Italy on Wednesday and Pope John Paul offered comfort to his widow.

Although he had no Italian blood, O'Dell's case aroused overwhelming public sympathy in a nation which strongly opposes the death penalty. Italy's prime minister and president had joined the Pope in vain appeals for his life.
A Vatican spokesman said Lori Urs, who married O'Dell a few hours before his death by lethal injection, spoke privately with Pope John Paul after attending his weekly general audience.
"The Pope met Mrs Urs for a few minutes and offered her some words of comfort," a Vatican spokesman said.
Rome airport officials said O'Dell's body arrived on a flight from Newark, New Jersey, and would be transferred to Palermo, Sicily later in the day.
O'Dell has been made an honorary citizen of the Sicilian capital, where he is due to be buried after a religious ceremony on Thursday.
He was executed despite widespread international protest, particularly in Italy, where he became a focal point for public opposition to capital punishment.
The country has no death penalty in civilian cases and is among the most vocal supporters of a worldwide ban. Italians mourned O'Dell like a native son or national hero.

O'Dell, 55, was convicted of the 1985 rape and murder of Helen Schartner, whose body was found in a field near some nightclubs he frequented. She had been pistol-whipped, raped, sodomised and strangled.
Schartner's family said they were annoyed and bewildered by the support the killer had received from Italians, who they felt had only seen one side of the story.
O'Dell's widow was accompanied to Italy by Sister Helen Prejean, his spiritual adviser and author of the best-selling book "Dead Man Walking".
The book, an account of the last days of a death row inmate, was made into a successful film starring Sean Penn and Susan Sarandon, who won an Oscar for her performance.
